_comment: A connector is DATA, never code. It says how to read a file, never WHERE that file is - the human picks it. Paths use dots for object keys and [] to walk an array. Nothing here is evaluated.
_verified: MEASURED against a real export on 2026-09-11: takeout-20260310T170953Z-3-001.zip, 558,450,834 bytes, member 'Takeout/Mon activite/Applications\u00a0Gemini/MonActivite.json' (12.7 MB), 2084 entries spanning 2025-01-21 to 2026-03-10. Every path and every prefix below was counted against that file, not recalled.
_folderTrap: The zip member name carries a NON-BREAKING SPACE in 'Applications\u00a0Gemini' and its accented characters are not stored as UTF-8. A caller that matches the member by exact name finds nothing. Match on a suffix instead.
_noThreads: There is no conversation id anywhere in this file: 'titleUrl' is absent from all 2084 rows, and two rows added from a shared link carry the SAME millisecond. Grouping by time proximity would invent threads rather than recover them, so grouping is 'none' and the reader reports turnsOnly.
_attachmentsNote: attachedFiles names sit beside MonActivite.json in the same folder of the archive (632 rows carry them). Reading those files is the caller's business; this connector only reports the names.

archive._prefixTrap: MEASURED, and the reason this is a LIST. The two real prompt prefixes do NOT share typography: 'Prompt' takes a NON-BREAKING space before its colon (1303 rows) while 'Discussion ajoutee...' takes an ordinary one (730 rows). 'Prompt: ' with a plain space matched 0 of 2084. A connector written against one spelling loses the other entirely.
humanPrefixes: Discussion ajoutée à partir du lien :
Discussion ajoutée à partir du lien :
archive._localeGap: Only the French spellings above are measured. The English ones are a best guess and may be wrong - which cannot fail silently, because a wrong guess shows up as a large 'no-prefix' count the app puts on screen. An unmeasured guess that the counter exposes is safer than an omission that loses every row.
archive._requirePrefixWhy: MEASURED: 51 rows carry a prefix that is NOT a prompt - 14 'Commentaires envoyes' (feedback the human sent to GOOGLE), 1 'Application utilisee', 1 Canvas item - plus 35 with no prefix at all. Kept raw, those would be filed as things the person typed to Gemini. They are skipped and counted instead.
archive._escapeNote: The prefixes are written as   / é escapes ON PURPOSE. Rendered literally, a non-breaking space is indistinguishable from an ordinary one in any editor, and the first reviewer to tidy up the 'double space' silently breaks 1303 of 2084 rows.

_mark: No vendor asset ships on this machine to trace, and drawing a lookalike under Google's name would be a fabricated brand asset. The label and tint stand in until an official path can be dropped in - a connector is data, so that costs no code change.
